title: A nested case-control study on the relationship between gut microbiota and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
summary: In a four-year nested case-control study of 404 adults (101 incident NAFLD cases and 303 controls), gut-microbiome and clinical features differed between groups. CatBoost predicted incident NAFLD with test AUC 0.762; the authors describe the result as exploratory, not causal or clinically ready.
ai_technology: CatBoost integrates baseline gut microbial species, metabolic pathways, and clinical indicators to predict incident NAFLD; a random-forest comparison and SHAP interpretation are also reported.
organization: First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University; Zhengzhou University; Huazhong University of Science and Technology

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; publication date and first result-bearing version checked.

evidence.tested: CatBoost used baseline microbiome, pathway and clinical features; a random-forest comparison and SHAP interpretation were reported.
evidence.unknown: Nested case-control prediction is exploratory; no causal inference, external transport validation or clinical readiness is established.
evidence.ai_role: CatBoost integrates baseline gut microbial species, metabolic pathways, and clinical indicators to predict incident NAFLD; a random-forest comparison and SHAP interpretation are also reported.
